title: Quercetin as a Potent Modulator of Innate and Adaptive Immunity: An In Vivo Evaluation in Wistar Rats | Journal of Natural Remedies
abstract:
Methods: Quercetin suspension was administered orally to rats at dose levels of 50,100 and 150mg/kg for 21days. The carbon clearance test, Delayed Type Hypersensitivity (DTH) reaction, and Hemagglutination Antibody (HA) titer were used to examine the immunomodulatory effect on both specific and non-specific immunity. Rats were given cyclophosphamide (100mg/kg p.o.) as an immunosuppression agent. In the processes of delayed type hypersensitivity response and hemagglutinating antibody titers, Sheep Red Blood Cells (SRBCs) were used as an antigen (0.1mL 20% SRBCs).
Delayed Type Hypersensitivity, Immunomodulation, Primary and Secondary Antibody Titer, Phagocytic Index, Quercetin · Background: The immune system maintains host defines through coordinated innate and adaptive responses, and its imbalance can lead to increased susceptibility to infections and inflammatory disorders.
Plant-derived flavonoids have attracted attention for their potential immunomodulatory properties. Quercetin, a naturally occurring flavonoid, has shown anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, but its effect on different arms of the immune response requires further experimental evaluation.
